Snapline 2.32.0

11 September 2026

  • Redaction: Blur and pixelate boxes are fully opaque everywhere, including over a window's drop shadow, a transparent region, and the box's own edges — and the box is solid while you are still dragging it out. Nothing of what is underneath survives into the export.
  • Exports keep the capture's density and colour: PNG, JPEG, HEIC and WebP exports now carry the Retina density and the display's colour profile they were captured with, so a P3 screenshot stays P3 and prints at the right size. Backgrounds are drawn in the same space.
  • Quick Access cards: Star works on recording and GIF cards. A card whose file was deleted retires instead of offering a dead drag. Escape after Use Keyboard on Latest Capture hands the keyboard back to the app you were in. The card panel is excluded from your own captures, and a lone “Checking…” card can be dismissed and times out on its own.
  • Pinned windows: Dragging a pin no longer steals keyboard focus from the app behind it; click a pin and Escape or ⌘W closes it. A pressed pin comes to the front. Pins are capped at eight.
  • Editor: Undo with a text box open no longer inserts a phantom step, and arrow-key nudges make one undo step per burst. Closing the editor cancels its background work. Opening a capture no longer claims unsaved changes. Double-click places no text box in the crop or eyedropper tools, and Smart Redact leaves the crop tool alone. Layer sliders scrub more smoothly, oversized backgrounds and layers are refused with a reason, and the canvas is readable by VoiceOver.
  • Recording: In a window recording, the camera bubble is recorded where you moved it. Taking a still during a recording keeps the desktop icons hidden. Display changes mid-take keep click highlights in place, and a keystroke or click overlay the system refuses is announced instead of silently missing.
  • Scrolling Capture: Finishing a tall capture uses about a third of the memory it did, and quitting while it is being saved waits for the file.
  • History: Deleting many captures, retention and export run in the background with progress and a Cancel button. Undo after a bulk delete restores everything, even if you started a second delete meanwhile. Deleting a starred capture from the status menu asks first and offers Undo Delete.
  • Capture-time Smart Redact: The unredacted shot stays out of your screenshots folder while the pass runs, and a capture interrupted mid-pass is recovered at next launch, redacted.
  • Settings: Return in the Reset All Settings dialog cancels instead of resetting. The shortcut recorder disarms when its window loses focus. The Advanced pane's Grant Access row matches onboarding.
  • Licensing: A renewal extends your existing license — no new key to paste; the app picks up the longer window on its next check. Deactivate on a Mac that only holds a receipt no longer burns the seat, and Return activates from the activation window.

Snapline 2.31.0

9 September 2026

  • Record Screen bar: Microphone and Camera are now split controls: one click turns each on or off, and the small chevron beside it opens the device menu, so you can pick which microphone to record and which camera the bubble shows. System Audio, Highlight Clicks and Show Keystrokes are toggles of their own. The bar no longer changes width while it is open, and everything fits under a window selection on a 13-inch display.
  • Camera bubble: Shape and border style moved onto the bubble itself. Hover it and three badges appear on its rim beside the resize handle: one flips between circle and rectangle, one shows the current border style and opens the presets menu, with Customize… leading to the full editor in Settings. Picking a camera from the bar turns the bubble on and swaps a live preview in place. The badges are off once recording starts; resizing still works mid-take.
  • Region selection: The size readout now appears only while you are drawing or resizing a region and steps aside once the size is settled, in Record Screen and Scrolling Capture alike.
  • Fixes: The pointer is an arrow over the Record Screen bar again, including its gaps and disabled controls, and switching modes no longer replaces the cursor another window had set.
  • Export location: In Settings → General, the export folder's path under Export location is now a link: click it, or the folder button beside it, to open that folder in Finder. If a custom folder is no longer reachable, the built-in one opens instead, as captures already fall back to it.

Snapline 2.30.0

8 September 2026

  • Open from Clipboard: Annotate an image you copied from a browser, Slack, Figma or Messages without saving it first. Choose Open from Clipboard in the menu bar, press ⌃⌘V anywhere, or press ⌘V on the History shelf; while the clipboard holds an image, the shelf also offers a Paste from clipboard tile. The image becomes an ordinary capture: History, the Editor, text recognition, pinning and export all apply. The clipboard is read only when you ask and is never watched.
  • Done copies your annotations: Done in the Editor now saves the marked-up capture and puts it on the clipboard, ready to paste. Turn it off under Settings → General → After annotating.
  • Camera bubble in window recordings: The camera bubble is no longer disabled for window recordings. It is composited over the recorded window, and its preview follows the window as you move it.
  • Help: The feature tour now covers trim, GIF options, polygons, emoji stickers and Layers.

Show your clicks and keys in screen recordings

  • Highlight Clicks: every mouse click draws a brief expanding ring at the pointer — dual-tone, so it reads against any background. Display and region recordings.
  • Show Keystrokes: the keys you press appear in a capsule at the bottom of the movie, with shortcuts in the same ⌃⌥⇧⌘ symbols as the Shortcuts pane. Needs the Input Monitoring permission, asked once at the toggle; a recording never fails over it — refused access just means no capsule, and Snapline says so.
  • Both overlays are drawn into the recorded frames, so trims, GIF conversions, and shares keep them. The toggles live in the Record Screen bar and Settings → Recording, are remembered, and ship off. Worth knowing: Show Keystrokes records what you type — ordinary text included — into the video.

Snapline 2.16.0

Capture with Self-Timer: frame the region first, watch the countdown, and the shot fires by itself.

Capture

  • Capture with Self-Timer. Frame the region first, then a visible countdown runs — and the shot fires by itself. The delay is for staging: open the menu or tooltip you want inside the frame while the timer counts. Selection works exactly like a normal region capture (releasing the drag starts the timer — no extra confirm), and the countdown sits inside the region with the seconds, an Esc hint, and a ✕ to cancel. Nothing steals focus, so the menu you stage stays open, and the countdown never appears in the shot.
  • Pick 3, 5, or 10 seconds from the new status-menu item beside the Self-Timer setting — its top row remembers your last-used delay for a one-click repeat — or bind a shortcut in Settings → Shortcuts (it ships unbound). A canceled timer saves nothing and says so.
  • The invisible delay is gone. If you keep a sticky Self-Timer default set, region and main-display captures now show this same live countdown instead of silently stalling before the crosshair — same delay, visible and cancellable.

Snapline 2.15.0

History learns starred captures. The relaunch now waits for the old copy to actually exit.

History

  • History learns starred captures. Star anything worth keeping and it survives the retention sweep unconditionally — it never expires, and a starred card asks before a manual delete goes through. Star from the card's hover control or its Star/Unstar menu item; a starred capture wears a badge at rest. The History toolbar gains a Starred filter that combines with search.

Robustness

  • Fixed: Snapline could quit itself and not come back after you answered the Screen Recording prompt. The relaunch waited a fixed half-second before reopening, which could fire while the old copy was still shutting down — so nothing came back, and no crash report explained it. The relaunch now waits for the old copy to actually exit, and when it can't reopen safely it stays running and tells you instead of vanishing. The prompt for one permission no longer triggers a relaunch offer for another.
  • Also fixed: the camera bubble no longer scans for cameras on the main thread, which could stall the Record Screen bar (and probe for nearby iPhones) each time it opened; its window now closes cleanly instead of racing an in-flight animation; and the bubble's style controls no longer risk a crash from a settings change or a removed gradient stop.
